recommendations.heading: 2.6 Variants and states are data attributes
recommendations.why: Matches the task through: component, contracts, data, attributes.
recommendations.excerpt: Modes, variants and states are data attributes (`data-variant`, `data-size` and `data-state`), not BEM modifier classes (epic Decision 4). A style restyles every variant and may change a component's inner markup. It never changes the contract: the same props, parts and `data-*` values exist in every style (#2416). A style that needs a new variant value, such as Studio's card variants or Bloom's notched widget, adds it to the component spec first, so every style can render it.

recommendations.heading: Customize Fresh UI
recommendations.why: Matches the task through: fresh, ui, component, contracts.
recommendations.excerpt: **Goal:** make the scaffolded frontend yours — edit a route, add an interactive island, restyle a component, install more UI primitives, and re-theme the app — without fighting the framework. NetScript scaffolds a real Fresh 2 application at `apps/dashboard/`, powered by the `@netscript/fresh` meta-framework, and the UI components live in *your* repository as copied source. After the copy, that code is yours to change. This is a task-oriented recipe. It assumes you already have a NetScript workspace (created with `netscript init`) whose `apps/dashboard/` app type-checks and runs. For the full

code.code:
netscript tokens init --app dashboard --preset studio-utility
netscript tokens build --app dashboard

# Add one component (or a named collection) to the dashboard app
netscript ui:add dropzone

# Add an AI / workspace primitive — e.g. the chat message renderer
netscript ui:add message

# Add a whole named collection in one call (theme + all its items)
netscript ui:add ai

recommendations.heading: Fresh UI & design
recommendations.why: Matches the task through: fresh, ui, component, contracts.
recommendations.excerpt: A design system earns its keep when the person — or agent — changing the UI can open every file involved. NetScript's Fresh UI layer is **copy-source**: components are installed into your repo as readable TypeScript and CSS you own, driven by design tokens you can edit, with a live gallery inside your own scaffolded app showing every primitive rendered with *your* tokens. Nothing in the visual layer hides behind a package boundary. ## Why copy-source, concretely The recurring failure in agent-edited UIs is not bad taste — it is a boundary.
